name: EPA ECHO sewer overflow and bypass event reports (eRule Phase 2 SOBE), Arizona permits
operator: US EPA (data filed by AZPDES permittees through ADEQ myDEQ / EPA eRule)
waters_covered: 42 AZPDES permits statewide; receiving water on 25 of 288 events (otherwise blank or an ADEQ assessment-unit code such as AZ15070101-210)
access_detail: Daily ZIP from ECHO (no auth). On 2026-11-07 the current-version ZIP (Last-Modified 2026-11-05) held only its metadata, so the module reads the current version of each report from the all-versions ZIP (all_sewer_overflow_and_collection_systems_tables.zip, 2026-11-04 extract). Tables: report and event (start/end datetime, duration, volume, lat/lon, structure type, description), types, receiving waters, causes, impacts, corrective actions; collection-system permits.

sample_record.sewer_overflow_bypass_description_text: SSO at [house number removed] N Tatum Blvd

cadence: ECHO file refreshed daily; received date a median 3 days (90th percentile 10 days) after start; five-day written report deadline
license: EPA public data; no licence restriction stated
legal_basis: 40 CFR 127 (eRule); AZPDES permit noncompliance reporting; A.A.C. R18-9-C305(F) for APP collection systems
status_reason: Read by the national eRule module (echo-sewer-overflow) with Arizona in its states since 2026-11-07: times in Phoenix time (the Navajo Nation's in its own daylight-saving time), ADEQ waterbody identifiers named, washes and canals read as waters, a shared point near the plant not used as the spill's. 2026-11-04 extract: 288 reports under Arizona permits from 42 permits and 52 Navajo Nation reports located in Arizona; 55 kept as reaching a water (27 SSO, 28 bypass), 285 dropped (257 with no evidence the sewage reached a water, 17 building backups, 10 bypasses held in the plant's ponds, lagoon or grounds, 1 naming only the plant's lagoon).
notes: 2026-11-04 extract: starts 2019-09-24 to 2026-10-28, received 2019-09-26 to 2026-10-30, a median 3 days after the start (90th percentile 10). Volume on 44 of 288 reports, coordinates on 285, an end on 287. Receiving-water entry on 25 reports (24 naming a water; one is UNK_PERNL), mostly as ADEQ waterbody identifiers (AZ15060202-421), which ADEQ's WBID layers name (Unnamed Trib to Munds Creek). Most reports give the plant's point (Grand Canyon South Rim 30 of 32 at one point). Timestamps carry no zone: read as America/Phoenix (no daylight time). Pima County (Tucson) has no reports, though EPA's collection-system table lists its systems; APP-only collection systems are not in this table. The Navajo Nation's permits (NN..., EPA Region 9) file here too: 56 reports, 52 located in Arizona (2024-02 to 2026-10), naming washes such as Black Creek Wash and Moenkopi Wash.

name: ADEQ waterbody identifier (WBID) layers, streams and lakes (ArcGIS Online)
access_detail: ArcGIS feature services of the adeq_gis account: STREAMS_WBID_AGOL (NAME, WBID, ORIGIN, TERMINUS, FLOWREGIME, CANAL) and LAKES_WBID_AGOL (NAME, WBID, TYPE); answered the project user agent on 2026-11-07 while azdeq.gov answers 403.
status_reason: Names the ADEQ waterbody identifiers Arizona permittees give as receiving waters in EPA's overflow reports (13 identifiers in the 2026-11-04 extract; EPA's ATTAINS holds 9 of them).
notes: Extract kept as data/reference/az-adeq-wbids.json (scripts/az_adeq_wbids.py): names only, no geometry.
